messages:
jess.support: Customer on Dedicated Private (VPC) is reporting outbound failures from their on-prem connector running in "no-internet" mode. They see 502s and TLS errors when the connector attempts to contact the Redwood control plane. Escalating for help. Summary + repro below.

jess.support: Repro steps from customer:
1) On their on-prem host (behind corporate proxy via PAC) run: `curl -v https://control.redwood.example/v1/models`
2) It fails with `SSL: certificate verify failed` or sometimes `ERROR: received HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway`.
3) `dig control.redwood.example` returns their corp DNS -> `10.10.10.1` (proxy-capturer)

jess.support: They provided a short capture: `openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.example:443 -servername control.redwood.example` returns cert with CN `corp-proxy.local` (i.e. TLS inspect). When we instruct them to `curl --proxy "" https://control.redwood.example` (bypass PAC) it times out (no direct internet).

jay.eng-infra: Thanks. Sounds like TLS interception + PAC forcing proxy. Two likely issues: 1) proxy is doing MITM (re-signing certs) -> client verifies and fails because CA not trusted; 2) proxy is doing SSL-terminate (not tunnel) for CONNECT -> SNI/ALPN stripped, downstream TLS handshake to Redwood fails.

leah.sre: Can we get a tcpdump showing the TLS ClientHello? Need to confirm if SNI is present and whether the proxy sends a CONNECT or issues its own TLS. Ask for `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/trace.pcap host control.redwood.example and port 443` or `sudo ngrep -W byline -d any "Host: |SNI"` for quick check.

maria.solutions: Also ask them for the PAC file snippet. Common misconfig: PAC returns `PROXY 10.10.10.1:8080` for `*.redwood.example` instead of `DIRECT` or `PROXY` with CONNECT tunneling. If proxy doesn't support CONNECT for that domain, it will fail.

jess.support: Customer posted PAC excerpt: `if (shExpMatch(host, "*.redwood.example")) return "PROXY 10.10.10.1:3128";` They said the proxy does TLS inspection for compliance.

jay.eng-infra: Ok. Immediate troubleshooting steps to give customer:
- Option A (fast): configure PAC to `DIRECT` or to return `PROXY ...` that supports CONNECT/TUNNEL for `*.redwood.example` so TLS is passthrough.
- Option B (if TLS inspect unavoidable): add our root CA to the connector's truststore (NOT ideal) and ensure the proxy preserves SNI and ALPN.
- Option C (network): allow egress to Redwood outbound IPs from the on-prem region via firewall rules and bypass the proxy for egress to those IPs.

leah.sre: Collect commands for them:
```
# check SNI from client side
openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.example:443 -servername control.redwood.example -alpn h2
# check what proxy returns
curl -v -x http://10.10.10.1:3128 https://control.redwood.example || true
# dns probe
dig +short control.redwood.example
```

jess.support: They ran `openssl` and posted output: cert subject CN=corp-proxy.local, issuer=Corp TLS MITM CA, TLS handshake completed but curl fails with `error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert certificate unknown` from the connector.

jay.eng-infra: That error means the connector process does not trust the proxy CA. Two paths: make the proxy tunnel TLS (preferred) or distribute the proxy CA into the connector truststore. For Private deployments the best practice is to avoid TLS inspection for Redwood control plane endpoints.

maria.solutions: Add note about egress allowlist: customers sometimes need to allow outbound to our managed control plane IPs. Provide them with IP ranges and DNS names. Example (customer-facing guidance):
- Domains to allow: `control.redwood.example`, `api.redwood.example`, `id.redwood.example`
- Sample IP ranges (advise to check latest): `3.122.45.0/24`, `52.14.210.0/24`, `34.207.128.0/24`

leah.sre: Also check for SNI stripping at the proxy: run this on their host and paste the output here: `tcpdump -A -s0 'tcp port 443 and host 10.10.10.1' | sed -n '1,120p'` — we want to see the TLS ClientHello SNI. If SNI is missing, proxy likely terminates and reoriginates without SNI.

jess.support: Customer responded: proxy does re-originate TLS and they cannot change that due to compliance. They asked: "Can Redwood support connectors behind intercepting proxies?"

jay.eng-infra: Short answer: yes, with caveats. Options: 1) configure the connector JVM/container to trust the proxy CA (we can provide steps for common connectors), 2) use an outbound peering/VPN so control traffic goes over a dedicated tunnel (bypasses corp proxy), 3) if connector supports explicit proxy and tunneling config, enable `useTunnel=true` so it issues CONNECT and preserves end-to-end TLS.

maria.solutions: I'll draft a small KB for them with exact steps per OS/container runtime. Include config snippets for system truststore, Java cacerts, and the connector environment variables to bypass PAC for the Redwood domains.

jess.support: Customer wants repro steps that they can run quickly. I gave them a checklist: 
- Run `openssl s_client -connect control.redwood.example:443 -servername control.redwood.example` and verify cert CN != corp-proxy.local (if CN==corp-proxy.local -> MITM).
- If MITM, try `curl -v --proxy "" https://control.redwood.example` to confirm no direct egress.
- If can't go direct, add proxy CA to truststore and retest.

leah.sre: I'll add an internal note: follow-up to engineering on whether the connector can expose a `--insecure-proxy-ca` flag for temporary testing (but not recommended for production). Filing a small spike to add clearer errors for MITM vs network timeouts. Tagging @incidents-bot to log escalation.

incidents-bot: Escalation logged: INC-2026-3152. Assigned to eng-infra for next-steps.

jess.support: Thanks all. I'll send the KB draft to the customer and request tcpdump + PAC file + connector logs. Will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:
